summary: Ludwik Skurzak was an Indology scholar who studied under Stanisław Schayer around 1930 to 1937. He served as a lecturer at the University of Breslau from circa 1946 to 1974.

Luigi Suali worked in Indology and philosophy, studying at the University of Bologna (~1899–1903) and under Hermann Jacobi (~1906–1908). He held a post at the University of Pavia from around 1909 to 1951.

Luis Oscar Gómez was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Puerto Rico, Yale University under Stanley Insler, and the University of Michigan. He held appointments at the University of Michigan (~1973–2008) and Mangalam Research Center (~2010–2017).

Luise Hercus was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Tollington School, St Anne's College, and the Australian National University, where she later held a post in South Asian and Buddhist Studies from circa 1969 to 1991.

Lungten Dubgyur specializes in Tibetology and other fields. He completed graduate studies at Sherubtse College, earned an LL.B from Government Law College, Mumbai, and obtained an LL.M from the University of Edinburgh.
Lungtok Tenpai Nyima was a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He founded Menri Monastery and served as its abbot and throne-holder from around 1969 to 2017.

Lynn A. Struve worked in Sinology and history/archaeology. She completed her studies at the University of Washington (~1963–1967) and the University of Michigan (~1968–1976), subsequently serving on the faculty at Indiana University from around 1977 to 2009.

Lynn Thomas is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Lancaster University and the University of Oxford (~1982–1987). She held a post as lecturer in Hinduism at the University of Roehampton.

Léon Feer worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, studying under Philippe-Édouard Foucaux. He held posts at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (1864), the Collège de France (1869–1872), and the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1872–1902).

Léon Vandermeersch was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at several Paris institutions and held posts at the University of Provence (~1966–1973), Paris Diderot University (~1973–1979), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1979–1993).
M. D. Balasubrahmanyam specialized in Indology and linguistics. He completed his dissertation studies at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1963–1969) and later held an academic post there.

M. H. Krishna was an Indologist and historian who studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore from circa 1908 to 1911. He served as Professor of History at the University of Mysore from around 1929 to 1947.
M. M. McCabe is a philosopher who studied at the University of Cambridge from circa 1967 to 1974. She later held a post at King's College London between approximately 1990 and 2014.

M. N. Srinivas worked in Indology and other fields, studying at Mumbai, under G. S. Ghurye, and Oxford. He held posts at Baroda College (~1951–1959), University of Delhi (~1959–1972), and the Institute for Social and Economic Change (~1972–1979).
M. R. Raghava Varier is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology. Educated at the University of Calicut, he served there as Reader in Epigraphy until his retirement.

M. S. Nagaraja Rao was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who studied at the University of Mysore (~1950–1955). He served as Director at the Department of Archaeology, Museums and Heritage from circa 1972 to 1984.

M. Seshagiri Sastri was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He served as Curator at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library and as Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Presidency University, Kolkata.

M. Shinoda is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Seiren Matsunami. Formal education includes studies at Agoura High School (~1991–1995) and Art Center College of Design (~1995–1998).

Mabel Haynes Bode was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Eduard Müller-Hess, Thomas William Rhys Davids, and Cecil Bendall. She held posts at University College London (~1908–1916) and SOAS (~1917–1920).
Madan Mohan Malaviya was an Indology scholar who founded Banaras Hindu University. He pursued his education at the University of Calcutta (~1879–1884) and the University of Allahabad (~1889–1891).
